From 8c88181ed452707f3815827225517b1964463b95 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jesper Dangaard Brouer <brouer@redhat.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Feb 2018 12:48:12 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] bpf: Sync kernel ABI header with tooling header for
 bpf_common.h

I recently fixed up a lot of commits that forgot to keep the tooling
headers in sync.  And then I forgot to do the same thing in commit
cb5f7334d479 ("bpf: add comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes"). Let correct
that before people notice ;-).

Lawrence did partly fix/sync this for bpf.h in commit d6d4f60c3a09
("bpf: add selftest for tcpbpf").

Fixes: cb5f7334d479 ("bpf: add comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes")
Signed-off-by: Jesper Dangaard Brouer <brouer@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>

diff --git a/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h b/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h
index 18be90725ab0..ee97668bdadb 100644
--- a/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h
+++ b/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h
@@ -15,9 +15,10 @@
 
 /* ld/ldx fields */
 #define BPF_SIZE(code)  ((code) & 0x18)
-#define		BPF_W		0x00
-#define		BPF_H		0x08
-#define		BPF_B		0x10
+#define		BPF_W		0x00 /* 32-bit */
+#define		BPF_H		0x08 /* 16-bit */
+#define		BPF_B		0x10 /*  8-bit */
+/* eBPF		BPF_DW		0x18    64-bit */
 #define BPF_MODE(code)  ((code) & 0xe0)
 #define		BPF_IMM		0x00
 #define		BPF_ABS		0x20
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h`**
   - Added comments to the definitions of `BPF_W`, `BPF_H`, and `BPF_B` to clarify their sizes:
     - `BPF_W` is now commented as "32-bit".
     - `BPF_H` is now commented as "16-bit".
     - `BPF_B` is now commented as "8-bit".
   - Added a comment for `BPF_DW` indicating it represents "64-bit" with the value `0x18`, although the actual definition for `BPF_DW` is not included in this patch.

### Relationships

- The modifications in `bpf_common.h` are intended to synchronize the kernel ABI header with the tooling header, addressing an oversight from a previous commit (`cb5f7334d479`) that added comments to BPF load/store sizes but did not update the corresponding tooling header. This patch ensures consistency between the kernel and tooling headers, which is crucial for maintaining compatibility and clarity in the BPF (Berkeley Packet Filter) implementation.

Here is the commit message:
bpf: Sync kernel ABI header with tooling header for
 bpf_common.h

I recently fixed up a lot of commits that forgot to keep the tooling
headers in sync.  And then I forgot to do the same thing in commit
cb5f7334d479 ("bpf: add comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes"). Let correct
that before people notice ;-).

Lawrence did partly fix/sync this for bpf.h in commit d6d4f60c3a09
("bpf: add selftest for tcpbpf").

Fixes: cb5f7334d479 ("bpf: add comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes")
Signed-off-by: Jesper Dangaard Brouer <brouer@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug was the failure to keep the tooling header (`bpf_common.h`) in sync with the kernel ABI header after a previous commit that added comments to the BPF load/store sizes. This inconsistency could lead to confusion or errors when developers refer to the definitions in the tooling header, as they would not match the expected values or comments in the kernel header.

-#define		BPF_W		0x00
-#define		BPF_H		0x08
-#define		BPF_B		0x10

+#define		BPF_H		0x08 /* 16-bit */
+#define		BPF_B		0x10 /*  8-bit */
+/* eBPF		BPF_DW		0x18    64-bit */
 #define BPF_MODE(code)  ((code) & 0xe0)
 #define		BPF_IMM		0x00

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
#define BPF_W		0x00
#define BPF_H		0x08
#define BPF_B		0x10
```
Reason:
These definitions in the tooling header (`bpf_common.h`) were not updated to include comments that explain the sizes associated with each BPF load/store operation after the previous commit. This inconsistency between the tooling header and the kernel ABI header could lead to confusion for developers, as they would not have the correct context or understanding of the values being used.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define BPF_W		0x00 /* 32-bit */
#define BPF_H		0x08 /* 16-bit */
#define BPF_B		0x10 /*  8-bit */
```
Reason:
These updated definitions now include comments that clarify the bit sizes associated with each BPF load/store operation. By synchronizing the tooling header with the kernel ABI header, the patch ensures that developers have the correct information, reducing the likelihood of errors or misunderstandings when working with these definitions.
